ui.meta.desc: An on-device deep convolutional network image upscaler: waifu2x and Real-ESRGAN weights all run locally, with a bicubic baseline and a pixel-level magnifier for comparison.

ui.ledger.title: Ledger
ui.loupe.note.zoom1: One cell maps exactly to one output pixel (1:1): whether the extra detail is filled in by the model or was there originally is clear from a direct comparison.
ui.loupe.note.zoomN: One cell = one output pixel × {z}; shows the look of "AI upscale", not its true pixels.
ui.loupe.note.far: Fits {size} into one cell (about 1:{z}) to observe overall structure; for single pixels press "1:1".
ui.loupe.note.same: Three cells, same block, same size.
ui.bic.note: The middle cell is computed live, only for the small block currently viewed, so any output size can be compared. Saving the full bicubic PNG is too costly, so it was not saved this time; the "size" row in the ledger is left blank.
ui.drawer.head: Upscale settings
ui.foot.body: Weights are the ONNX versions of waifu2x (CUnet / Swin-UNet), Real-ESRGAN, and AnimeSharp; all run on this machine, and images never leave it.
ui.foot.summary: Two limitations that must be stated
ui.foot.p1: One: the waifu2x family produces wrong results on DirectML. No error is raised, but the output is garbled. Therefore, at load time the program runs the same input once on the GPU and once on the CPU, compares the values, and falls back to CPU on mismatch; the conclusion is cached in models/.device_probe.json. Real-ESRGAN and AnimeSharp run normally on DirectML and stay on the GPU.
ui.foot.p2: Two: each family has different input/output conventions. waifu2x drops a ring of border pixels (CUnet is out = 2×in − 72, Swin is out = 2×in − 32), while the Real-ESRGAN family is clean out = 4×in. At startup the program probes two sizes with a small image, fits out = a×in + b, and from that decides padding and cropping; no magic numbers are hard-coded.
ui.noscript: This page relies on JavaScript to call the local inference interface; enable JavaScript in your browser.
ui.engine.note.dml: This machine has DirectML, but the waifu2x family weights produce wrong results on it; at load time the program does one GPU/CPU numeric comparison and falls back to CPU on mismatch. Real-ESRGAN and AnimeSharp stay on the GPU.

ui.ledger.scale.native: Network native ×{native}, so it is chained {passes} times; the gap is filled to ×{scale} by Lanczos.
ui.ledger.scale.one: One network pass reaches the target scale; no extra interpolation.
ui.ledger.clear.note: The network output edges are gradient transitions; this step only pulls the edges back in. Flat areas are unchanged, so no noise is ground in.
ui.ledger.clear.none: This level applies no sharpening; the output is the network's raw result.
ui.ledger.bright.note: This step makes the output slightly brighter than the original, in exchange for the airy look of the online version; it is not closer to the original. To stay closest, switch back to "As-is".
ui.ledger.bright.none: Brightness unchanged; output matches the original's luminance.
ui.ledger.mps.note: Output pixels divided by pure inference time. This machine is {dev}, so the value is its real speed.
ui.ledger.ssim.note: The result is scaled back to the original size and compared with it. Closer to 1 means less change to the content; a clear drop means the model is inventing content.
ui.ledger.sharpness.note: Ratio of Laplacian-response variance within the same 512×512 region. Original {src}, bicubic {bic}.
ui.ledger.bytes.note: Both are PNG lossless. The extra size is the detail the model filled in and the noise it brought out.
ui.ledger.bytes.skip: Output {mp} MP; encoding the full bicubic PNG once just to get the size is too costly, so it is skipped. The middle cell of the magnifier is computed live on demand and is unaffected; it can be viewed normally.
ui.ledger.recovered: This is an old result recovered while organizing the output directory — its log was not kept, so time and sharpness metrics cannot be recomputed and show "—"; size and bytes are read from the file itself.
